ops.title: RESOLVED in v0.58.2-v0.58.5: event-driven overlay convergence and File Provider mutation/anchor fixes

ops.body:
Resolved and deployed to **yBook-Pro** and **yasyf-home** on 2026-07-16. Both CLI and `CCPoolStatus.app` are at **v0.58.5 (9e9d74f)**. The rollout hot-swapped the daemon/app without replacing the detached mount holder and preserved every live Claude PID observed across each upgrade boundary.

## Final diagnosis

The v0.55.0 incident was not one bug. It was a stack of independent sources of churn whose symptoms overlapped:

1. **Routine overlay convergence did unnecessary provider work.** Session discovery, overlay health, semantic content changes, and provider reconciliation were coupled to ticker passes. A healthy row could be rechecked/reconciled without a new fact that made it dirty. File Provider paid for this most visibly because a control-plane lookup/signal can wake an appex, but the wasted work applied to every backend.
2. **File Provider mutations contained nested coordination.** Extension callbacks already execute under fileproviderd's access claim, but the extension wrapped backing writes in `NSFileCoordinator`. That could deadlock `deleteItem`, produce `NSFileProviderErrorDomain -1005`, and leave fileproviderd retrying or relaunching the appex.
3. **Computed-item reannouncement expired every sync anchor.** The old `ComputedReannouncement.invalidate` mutated the single stored anchor. Every legitimate computed-content update therefore forced `syncAnchorExpired` (`NSFileProviderErrorDomain -1004`) and a full re-enumeration instead of returning a bounded change set.
4. **Trash was accidentally advertised as supported.** File Provider tried to move files through `.Trash`; the provider cannot represent that location and should have returned `NSFeatureUnsupportedError` immediately.
5. **`procscan` treated a disappearing PID as a whole-scan failure.** `KERN_PROCARGS2` can return EIO after an appex exits between enumeration and inspection. That PID is not a Claude session; aborting the scan converted harmless process churn into false fleet-wide busy state.

The original acct-16 `settings.json` -1005 was a transient File Provider operation failure, not a missing file. The backing and mounted files were present and readable. There has been no recurrence after removing nested coordination and anchor invalidation.

## Durable architecture (v0.58.2)

Commit **a7113309** made convergence event-driven for all backends:

- One daemon-wide 5-second session heartbeat performs the process scan once and publishes a snapshot to every consumer. Per-feature rescans were removed. Per-PID EIO/ENOENT/ESRCH now skips only the exited PID.
- A kqueue vnode watcher marks only semantic input causes: canonical `.claude.json`, shared `settings.json`, shared top-level structure, and companion-app replacement. Atomic replacement is covered by watching both the file and its parent.
- Semantic stamps normalize content before hashing. Formatting-only and private-only writes do not advance a global generation.
- A persisted per-account applied-generation ledger makes routine work a no-op when backend, canonical, settings, structure, and app generations match.
- Symlink rows merge canonical JSON only when its semantic stamp changes. FUSE consumes content through the live bridge and reconciles only when structure/backend state changes. File Provider calls `NotifyContent` only when its semantic generation changes. Healthy rows on **all** backends skip routine `Check`, `Reconcile`, and `SyncOverlay` work.
- A newly active or explicitly selected account still receives an on-demand catch-up and structural health check. That is a correctness gate caused by a session transition, not periodic maintenance.
- Healthy File Provider domains receive zero maintenance probes. Deep probes run only for domains already marked wedged/parked and are backoff-gated.

A real shared semantic change can still produce a short all-active-domain File Provider signal burst: every computed `.claude.json` includes the shared base, so all of those generations genuinely changed. That is bounded, causal work. Account-private writes are domain-local.

## File Provider correctness train

- **v0.58.3 / 03449a36:** advertises trash as unsupported and returns the exact feature-unsupported error; `.trash` retries stopped.
- **v0.58.4 / f963a2ad:** removes every extension-side `NSFileCoordinator`; backing mutation uses direct atomic rename/remove/copy under fileproviderd's existing claim. Fresh live deletes completed in 2-90 ms instead of wedging.
- **v0.58.5 / 9e9d74fb:** replaces the single mutable anchor with 32 bounded versioned snapshots plus a one-shot forced-update set. Old valid anchors remain enumerable; computed changes are returned as updates without `syncAnchorExpired`.

## Validation

Build and test gates for v0.58.5 were clean: 63 Swift tests, signed File Provider app build, `scripts/test.sh ./...`, race suite, `go vet ./...`, pure-Go build, and golangci-lint. Branch CI and the signed/notarized release workflow completed successfully; the tap published v0.58.5.

Live post-bootstrap windows on yBook-Pro showed:

- zero `sync_anchor_expired`
- zero extension internal errors
- zero cc-pool File Provider probe/prepare failures
- zero trash failures
- no `CCPoolStatus: fp_probe` activity
- successful backup create/delete and `.claude.json` jobs completing in milliseconds

The previously suspicious `CCPoolStatus` XPC rate was not a continuous 12-18/sec app/widget loop. The remaining entries occur in short bursts of `file provider manager connection invalidated` aligned with real semantic `.claude.json`/backup mutations and enumerator signals. Unified logs show the fileproviderd snapshot mutations before the appex launches. They are event-driven work, not the old 10-second probe hammer. `extension request grace timer ran out` after a completed job is normal idle teardown, not a stuck request.

On yasyf-home, post-bootstrap validation showed one expected v1-to-v2 anchor migration expiry, then zero further anchor expiries and no app XPC loop. Sampled `settings.json` reads succeeded on both machines, including acct-17.

## Operational result

No account-specific repair, migration off File Provider, `authdb`, or `tccutil` action was needed. The original guardrails remain in force. The incident is closed at v0.58.5.

Cross-refs: [[89382e69]] (the prematurely clean v0.55.0 ship validation), [[0a067986]] (ENOMEM and original probe-hammer mechanism), [[22128082]] (Stage-2 verdict/W-X1).
